api-control-plane.title: From a Deployment declaration to a running Pod
api-control-plane.caption: API-mediated reconciliation is asynchronous. Controllers, scheduler and kubelet use the API; the linear path is a responsibility sequence, not direct calls from controller to scheduler.

services-dns.title: A banking request takes the data-plane path
services-dns.caption: The client resolves the name, then sends traffic through the implemented data plane. DNS does not proxy the HTTP request. The API supplies configuration; it is not on the application packet path.

probes.title: Probe failure has different consequences
probes.caption: Readiness and liveness are independent after startup succeeds. A restart is not the action for readiness failure. Endpoint changes are asynchronous.

identity-rbac.title: Three separate gates for an API write
identity-rbac.caption: An authenticated caller can be forbidden; an authorized write can be rejected by admission. An accepted object can still fail to become a healthy workload.

storage.title: Storage follows a lifecycle beyond one container
storage.caption: This example shows delayed binding. Other classes can bind immediately. The backup is a separate responsibility; a mounted volume is not a verified restore.

rollouts.title: Rolling update with two desired replicas
rollouts.caption: Assumes maxSurge 1 and maxUnavailable 0. Spare schedulable capacity is required. Rollback changes the workload template, not external database effects.

network-policy.title: A connection needs both relevant directions allowed
network-policy.caption: DNS and the enforcing implementation are dependencies, not policy objects that automatically run in sequence. Test both allowed and denied clients. Policies do not create listeners.

cluster-internals.title: Control-plane state versus node execution
cluster-internals.caption: Control-plane components coordinate through API state. etcd is not the bank application database. Placement and execution are separate responsibilities.

etcd-recovery.title: A recoverable service needs several checkpoints
etcd-recovery.caption: These are separate recovery inputs. An etcd snapshot alone does not contain image binaries, every volume or external service state.

gateway-api.title: Ownership and reference boundaries in Gateway API
gateway-api.caption: Route attachment and cross-namespace backend permission are separate checks. The configured data plane must actually serve a request; declarations and status are complementary evidence.

gcp-network.title: Trace two different outbound destinations
nodes: No external address on the instance
gcp-network.caption: The two branches are alternatives by destination and configuration. This simplified map excludes Private Service Connect and private services access, which have different purposes. Neither route bypasses application authentication.

gke-identity.title: Workload identity and resource authorization
nodes: Grant objectViewer on the dummy bucket
gke-identity.caption: This illustrates direct principal access. IAM service-account impersonation is a separate supported pattern, not an extra mandatory step. Runtime identity does not come from downloading a key.

gcp-delivery.title: Promote the same artifact with separate authority
nodes: Run tests and build the image
gcp-delivery.caption: Build and release identities have different responsibilities. Provenance and scanning support trust decisions; they do not replace application tests or database migration planning.

gcp-recovery.title: Several independent inputs rebuild one service
nodes: Known data and real request checks
gcp-recovery.caption: An etcd or GKE backup alone is not a complete banking service recovery. The target environment, keys, quotas and external dependencies must be available and tested.

gcp-events.title: Retry without duplicating a business effect
nodes: Read stored result; avoid duplicate effect
gcp-events.caption: The duplicate-delivery branch requires application/storage logic. A messaging feature does not atomically cover arbitrary external side effects.

gcp-ai.title: Permission-aware retrieval with an evaluation boundary
gcp-ai.caption: Retrieval is not proof of truth. No step grants account access or transfer authority. Offline test cases describe expected behaviour; actual model performance requires execution evidence.

gke-network.title: Separate desired routing from serving a request
gke-network.caption: Control-plane reconciliation and client traffic are different paths. Exact backend and load-balancer resources depend on the chosen supported GKE implementation.

gcp-hierarchy.title: Hierarchy inheritance and separate billing linkage
gcp-hierarchy.caption: Billing is shown separately from hierarchy. Effective access can include inherited grants and constraints; folder placement is not a billing transfer.

gcp-migration.title: A cutover has a write boundary
gcp-migration.caption: Before target writes, aborting may be simple. After target writes, changing traffic alone is insufficient: data authority and reconciliation must be resolved.

gcp-data.title: Illustrative transfer transaction and reporting boundary
gcp-data.caption: This is a proposed business design, not implemented banking functionality. Precise transaction, event-publication and reconciliation semantics must be designed and tested for the selected database.

orientation.title: Different layers own different outcomes
orientation.caption: Kubernetes coordinates execution. The business-correctness box is a separate responsibility that replica management cannot supply.

terminal.title: Read a manifest through three kinds of validation
nodes: Cluster policy may reject a write
terminal.caption: Parsing, dry-run and runtime testing establish different facts. Server-side dry-run does not persist the workload or execute its containers.

setup.title: The local cluster has nested execution layers
nodes: Submits requests to the lab API
setup.caption: This is a local learning topology. It does not create independent physical failure domains or native cloud load balancers.

starter.title: Selectors connect independent declarations
starter.caption: A Service selector does not create Pods. The localhost port-forward is a learning access path; it does not demonstrate an external load balancer.

objects-contexts.title: Scope, grouping and ownership are different axes
objects-contexts.caption: Labels group objects; ownerReferences establish ownership. Cluster-scoped resources sit outside namespace containment.

images.title: Build inputs become content-addressed runtime artifacts
images.caption: A digest identifies bytes; it does not prove security. Runtime filesystem changes do not modify the original registry image.

pod-design.title: Pod replacement differs from a container restart
nodes: May restart container in same Pod
Creates new Pod with new UID
pod-design.caption: Controller replacement is a separate response when the managed Pod is removed or replaced. Restarting a container does not change the Pod UID.

init-sidecars.title: Initialization and a native sidecar have different lifetimes
init-sidecars.caption: This example deliberately puts a regular init before a native sidecar. A native sidecar continues running; it does not need to exit successfully before the application starts.

workload-choice.title: Choose a controller from the work requirement
nodes: What identity and lifetime are needed?
workload-choice.caption: Controllers are alternatives for different needs. StatefulSet identity alone does not replicate a database or prove safe failover.

jobs.title: Scheduling and processing need separate duplicate controls
jobs.caption: CronJob scheduling is not an exactly-once business guarantee. A concurrency policy does not replace durable idempotency.

configuration.title: Configuration reaches containers in different ways
configuration.caption: Updating a ConfigMap object alone does not necessarily roll out Pods or reload application settings. Choose and verify a configuration delivery strategy.

secrets.title: A Secret crosses several protection boundaries
nodes: Who may read or change it?
secrets.caption: Base64 is encoding, not encryption. Restrict workload creation and node access as well as direct Secret reads; never publish credential payloads in evidence.

resources.title: Requests, limits and admission answer different questions
nodes: Exceeding limits may lead to OOM
resources.caption: Scheduling acceptance does not prove enough runtime capacity. CPU throttling and memory OOM are different mechanisms with different symptoms.

security-context.title: Restrict execution while keeping required paths usable
nodes: UID, successful work and denied write
security-context.caption: Do not force restrictions onto an incompatible image without adapting required paths and permissions. A policy setting needs observed workload evidence.

debugging.title: Choose evidence from the failing lifecycle stage
debugging.caption: These evidence sources complement one another; follow the branch matching the symptom. Logs alone cannot explain a Pod that never started.

ingress.title: An Ingress declaration needs an implementation
ingress.caption: An Ingress resource by itself does not install a controller. Controller-specific annotations and capabilities are not portable Kubernetes guarantees.

release-strategies.title: Separate deployment from traffic allocation
release-strategies.caption: Blue/green can switch traffic between environments; a canary sends a controlled subset. Replica ratios alone are not a precise request-weight guarantee.

helm.title: Helm records releases but does not remove workload risk
helm.caption: A Helm rollback does not undo external database effects. Rendering and linting cannot prove runtime health; verify the deployed application.

kustomize.title: A base becomes an environment through explicit patches
kustomize.caption: Kustomize transforms manifests without a template language. Review the output because changed labels, names and selectors can alter relationships.

extensions.title: Schema extension is not a running controller
nodes: An instance of the registered kind
extensions.caption: The sample BankReport CRD registers data only. Without a controller, creating a BankReport does not generate a report.

api-versions.title: Separate served API versions from stored resources
api-versions.caption: Changing only apiVersion may be insufficient when fields or semantics changed. A future upgrade can remove an endpoint still present today.

kubeadm.title: Bootstrap trust before expecting a working workload
kubeadm.caption: kubeadm does not provision the VMs or select every infrastructure component. NotReady after join can reflect missing networking rather than a bad token.

availability.title: Independent redundancy and quorum checks
availability.caption: Stacked etcd may colocate datastore and API roles. Three software replicas are not necessarily three independent physical failure domains.

upgrades.title: An upgrade needs preconditions and acceptance gates
nodes: Drain, upgrade and return one node
upgrades.caption: Exact package operations and ordering must follow the official guide for the actual transition. Do not copy a current-version installer into an unrelated older cluster.

extension-interfaces.title: Extension contracts solve different integration problems
extension-interfaces.caption: This is a responsibility map, not a universal direct-call trace. CSI also includes controller-side services. An Operator is not a replacement for CRI, CNI or CSI.

admin-rbac.title: Access and delegation require separate reviews
admin-rbac.caption: RBAC grants are additive; a narrow Role does not cancel a broader grant. Workload creation can also expose powerful identities or data, so evaluate indirect access.

scheduling.title: Feasibility precedes placement preference
scheduling.caption: A toleration permits consideration of a tainted node; it does not force placement there. Storage topology and admission can add further constraints.

autoscaling.title: Two scaling loops can have different blockers
nodes: Observed CPU or other supported signal
autoscaling.caption: CPU utilisation targets depend on requests. HPA does not create nodes by itself, and adding nodes cannot fix incompatible placement or a serial database bottleneck.

disruptions.title: Draining uses voluntary eviction controls
disruptions.caption: Replacement and shutdown can overlap and are asynchronous. A disruption budget does not stop involuntary node failure or guarantee zero user errors.

cni-dataplane.title: Service traffic uses programmed networking state
cni-dataplane.caption: The API is a source of configuration, not a hop for ordinary application packets. eBPF-based implementations can replace selected forwarding mechanisms; behaviour still requires validation.

coredns.title: DNS resolution is one dependency in a request path
coredns.caption: DNS answers do not proxy the HTTP request. NXDOMAIN, timeout and an application error are distinct observations; confirm the namespace and query form.

csi-storage.title: Locate the failed storage lifecycle boundary
csi-storage.caption: Not every driver requires an attachment stage. Capacity fields, mounting and application-consistent restoration are different verification boundaries.

node-triage.title: A node symptom needs host-level evidence
nodes: Disk, memory, CPU, PIDs and time
node-triage.caption: Read-only evidence comes before a controlled repair. A reboot can hide the cause; retain logs and explain recurring resource growth.

control-plane-triage.title: Diagnose access before editing control-plane state
control-plane-triage.caption: These are diagnostic branches, not a requirement to edit every layer. Keep static-manifest backups outside the watched directory.

network-triage.title: Trace a failed request from name to response
network-triage.caption: Do not treat all timeouts as one cause. Compare direct backend and Service paths where permitted, then inspect external layers if they exist.

observability.title: Signals answer different diagnostic questions
observability.caption: Signals are complementary, not interchangeable. Missing telemetry is not zero failure; minimise sensitive data and excessive cardinality.

ckad-capstone.title: Developer evidence loop
nodes: No copied solution during the task
Explain gaps, not only final status
ckad-capstone.caption: Offline reasoning and live execution provide different evidence. Record unperformed tasks honestly; a timer or completion mark is not certification.

cka-capstone.title: Administrator evidence loop
nodes: No copied solution during the task
Explain gaps, not only final status
cka-capstone.caption: Offline reasoning and live execution provide different evidence. Record unperformed tasks honestly; a timer or completion mark is not certification.

gcp-capstone.title: Cloud engineer / architect evidence loop
nodes: No copied solution during the task
Explain gaps, not only final status
gcp-capstone.caption: Offline reasoning and live execution provide different evidence. Record unperformed tasks honestly; a timer or completion mark is not certification.

gcp-start.title: Scope and billing checks precede provisioning
nodes: Inform recipients; not a spending cap
gcp-start.caption: Default CLI configuration can be overridden by command flags. Budget alerts, quotas and deliberate resource cleanup solve different problems.

gcp-iam.title: Explain an access decision without using broad roles
gcp-iam.caption: Service-account impersonation authority must also be reviewed. A project-local policy is not necessarily the complete effective access picture.

gcp-compute.title: Select an operating model from requirements
nodes: State, runtime, scale and team skills
gcp-compute.caption: The three platforms are alternatives or complementary roles. The GKE course choice is a learning objective, not proof that every information page needs Kubernetes.

gcp-storage.title: Retention and recovery affect deletion outcomes
gcp-storage.caption: Features and costs depend on configuration and current service rules. A successful delete of a current object is not always removal of every retained copy.

gke-modes.title: Platform mode changes the ownership boundary
gke-modes.caption: Modes have shared and distinct responsibilities. Inspect current support and admitted settings instead of assuming local kind behaviour is identical.

gke-first.title: Cloud provisioning and Kubernetes access are separate gates
nodes: Ready Pods, endpoints and page marker
gke-first.caption: Node identity is not automatically the application identity. Learning commands do not provision anything until the learner explicitly runs them in their own project.

gke-lifecycle.title: Maintenance depends on both policy and spare capacity
gke-lifecycle.caption: Maintenance controls do not promise indefinite upgrade avoidance. A strict disruption budget cannot manufacture healthy replicas or spare capacity.

gcp-iac.title: State links configuration with real resources
gcp-iac.caption: A plan is not an executed result. Protect state and locking, and review drift, destructive replacements and costs before applying.

gcp-observe.title: Define the denominator before trusting the SLO
gcp-observe.caption: A request-based objective is not a fixed downtime allowance. Missing data, exclusions and telemetry health must be explicitly handled.

gcp-security.title: Match controls to an actual threat boundary
nodes: What is valuable and how misused?
gcp-security.caption: Controls are complementary. Encryption does not prevent an authorised principal from requesting plaintext; compliance needs actual requirements and evidence.

gcp-cost.title: Cost improvement must preserve required outcomes
nodes: Unit cost and quality after change
gcp-cost.caption: Use current regional prices and dated assumptions. A cheaper unit is not necessarily a cheaper completed task, and resource deletion may leave retained costs.

gcp-architecture.title: A defensible decision connects requirements to evidence
nodes: Test claims and define revisit triggers
gcp-architecture.caption: A component diagram alone does not explain why a choice is appropriate. Distinguish an implemented learning sample from a proposed future banking platform.
